$comment: Allow-list for scripts/check-orphan-assets.mjs — assets that ARE unreferenced and
are supposed to be. Every entry is an object with a "path" and a "reason"; a bare
path string, or a reason shorter than five words, fails the check itself. An
allow-list nobody has to justify is how this repo's stale manifests started, and a
list of bare paths cannot be audited later by anyone who was not in the room.
"path" is either an exact repo-relative file path, or a directory prefix ending in
'/'. Prefer exact paths: a directory prefix silently absolves whatever gets added
next to the file you meant.
An entry suppresses the --check failure and annotates the report. It does NOT hide
the file: report mode still lists it, now with its reason attached, which is the
point — the next cleanup reads the reason instead of re-deriving it.
